\subsection{Program Societies}
\label{program-societies}

\begin{enumerate}
\item

  The MES recognizes the following program societies:

  \item

  \item

    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Engineering Physics Society (EPS)
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    iBioMed Society (iBMS)
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Materials Science and Engineering Society (MSES)
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    McMaster Engineering and Management Society (MEMS)
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}

  \end{enumerate}

\subsection{Clubs}
\label{clubs}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  A Club shall be an organization composed of at least 75\% McMaster undergraduate students in the Faculty of Engineering.
  \end{quote}
\item

  A Club may receive funding from the MES by following the procedures set out in MES Bylaws Section \ref{clubs-and-teams-funding-policy}.

\subsection{Teams}
\label{teams}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  A Group is considered to be a Team if they are a non-sporting organization composed of at least 75\% McMaster undergraduate students in the Faculty of Engineering which competes at external events as representatives of McMaster.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  In order to receive Team status, teams must have competed in at least one external event the previous year, or be approved by the MES council for extenuating circumstances. Otherwise, the group will be transferred to Club status.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  In order to maintain Team status, they are at minimum required to:
  \end{quote}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Host events and maintain a social media presence
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Present an accountability presentation at one of the General Meetings

\subsection{Affiliates}
\label{affiliates}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  An affiliate shall be an organization composed of at least 75\% McMaster undergraduate students in the Faculty of Engineering.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  An affiliate is a collection of people who wish to be recognized by the MES and do not require funding.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  Affiliates are a stepping stone for new groups to eventually reach ratification as a club or team.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  In order to maintain affiliate status with the MES, they are at minimum required to:
  \end{quote}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Host events and maintain a social media presence
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Present an accountability presentation at Council, once every academic year
    \end{quote}

    \begin{enumerate}
    \item
      \begin{quote}
      Recently affiliated groups are not required to present at Council until the following academic year
      \end{quote}
    \end{enumerate}
  \end{enumerate}

\subsection{Affiliates Process}
\label{affiliates-process}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  To become an MES Affiliate, you must email the DoC your intent to become an MES Affiliate and have a meeting with DoC
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  After meeting with the DoC, all intending MES Affiliates must put forth a motion for affiliation at a Council Meeting. Council will vote on the motion and the DoC will assist you with the next steps whatever the result.
  \end{quote}
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Ratification Process}
\label{ratification-process}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  To become an MES Group, you must be an MES Affiliate for at least one year, then let the DoC know your intent to apply to be an MES Group.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  Each MES Affiliate intending to become an MES Group must present a motion to MES Council to be recommended to the General Meeting. Upon a majority vote from Council, the MES Affiliate must submit a motion for ratification at the second General Meeting in a given academic year (See MES Bylaws Section \ref{general-meetings-sagm}).
  \end{quote}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    On a majority vote at the General Meeting, the MES Affiliate will be ratified as a Group recognized by the MES.
    \end{quote}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    Motions may be put forth at the first General Meeting in a given academic year only by direct permission from the DoC.
    \end{quote}
  \end{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  Long-established groups may be able to bypass the affiliation stage and become directly ratified as an MES Group.
  \end{quote}

  \begin{enumerate}
  \item
    \begin{quote}
    This follows the same ratification process for MES Affiliates, wherein Council will motion whether to send the group to the Semi Annual General Meeting for ratification.
    \end{quote}
  \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{De-Affiliation Process}
\label{de-affiliation-process}

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  If an Affiliate is not performing or achieving certain standards, they may be de-affiliated.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The de-affiliation process will occur at Council.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC shall be responsible for compiling a list of Affiliates that shall undergo the de-affiliation process. A motion for de-affiliation may be proposed at the discretion of the DoC, but reasons could include that the affiliate did not fulfil requirements listed in Section \ref{affiliates}.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC will be responsible for communicating with Affiliates that may be facing de-affiliation
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC will present to Council all Groups that shall under-go the de-affiliation process, and the vote for de-affiliation will be made during Council.
  \end{quote}
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{De-Ratification Process}
\label{de-ratification-process}

If a group is not performing or achieving certain standards, they may be de-ratified.

\begin{enumerate}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The de-ratification process will occur at the Winter General Meeting.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC shall be responsible for compiling a list of groups that shall undergo the de-ratification process. A motion for de-ratification may be proposed at the discretion of the DoC, but reasons could include that the Group that the Club or Team did not fulfill requirements listed in Section \ref{clubs} or \ref{teams}
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC will be responsible for communicating with groups that may be facing de-ratification.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  The DoC will present to Council all groups that shall under-go the de-ratification process, and, upon approval from Council, these groups shall be presented and voted for de-ratification at the Winter General Meeting.
  \end{quote}
\item
  \begin{quote}
  Clubs and Teams may all be subject to the de-ratification process
  \end{quote}
\end{enumerate}
